_why: Ratchet. A price can fail to match for honest reasons: it is attributed to something other than a vendor page, or the source renders client-side. Baselined so only NEW breakage fails. EDIT BY REMOVAL ONLY -- adding an entry silences a real claim.

vs/outlier-vs-cline/index.html.$6.80: The page itself says this is user-reported in cline/cline issue #7558 and explicitly NOT a vendor statement. GitHub renders issue bodies client-side, so a curl of the cited URL cannot contain it. The claim is correctly attributed on the page; the gate cannot see the source.

_why_additions_2026_09_16: Three entries added 2026-09-16, against this file's own edit-by-removal rule, and here is the argument so it can be challenged. Neither is a vendor price the gate could ever match: one is a component market price, two are press-reported figures the page itself says the vendor does not publish. They are gate CATEGORIES that do not exist yet, not silenced claims. If either category ever gets modelled, remove these.

vs/outlier-vs-jan/index.html.$375: Not a rival's price at all. The page says '32 GB of DDR5 running around $375 as an AI-driven shortage squeezes PC building', attributed to a June 3 2026 report. A component market price is a different claim class from a vendor subscription, and no vendor pricing page will ever carry it.

vs/outlier-vs-meta-ai/index.html.$7.99: The page states 'Meta publishes no price' and labels these 'Press coverage in May 2026 reported $7.99 and $19.99 a month ... reported, not confirmed on a Meta page.' Demanding a vendor citation for a price the vendor does not publish is impossible by construction, and flagging it PENALISES the page for disclosing its own provenance. Same shape as the cline $6.80 entry above.
